verdict.rationale: Lium documents its own official SDK on a dedicated SDK page. The SDK rents the cheapest matching node, runs a function there, returns the result, and removes the pod or keeps it warm. It is installed from a first-party package (`pip install lium.io`). The OpenAPI type generation in lium-docs-20 is a developer building block, not an official SDK, so it is not credited here. missing for 10: evidence of SDKs beyond the single (apparently Python) package, in-depth SDK reference documentation, independent or hands-on corroboration of the SDK itself.
